images.title: Taking away groups of 6 from 378 coconuts
images.purpose: Show 378 coconuts as blocks of groups of 6 that are taken away: three blocks of 20 groups and one block of 3 groups.
images.composition: One long bar made of four blocks with the total above it and a label for each block under it.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. One bar of four rectangles joined end to end, 100 px high, at y 220 to 320, x 128 to 1328, with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline on each. Block 1: x 128 to 509, teal #0072B2, white label 120 (56 px). Block 2: x 509 to 890, teal, white label 120. Block 3: x 890 to 1271, teal, white label 120. Block 4: x 1271 to 1328, amber #E69F00, dark label 18 (36 px). Above the bar a grey #6B7280 bracket (4 px) spans x 128 to 1328 at y 190 with the label 378 centred above it at x 728 and y 145 (56 px, dark). Under blocks 1, 2 and 3, centred at x 318, 699 and 1080 and at y 380, the label 20 groups of 6 (40 px, dark). Under block 4 a short grey line (4 px) runs from x 1300, y 320 down to y 440 and the label 3 groups of 6 (40 px, dark) is centred at x 1200 and y 480. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: Taking away groups of the divisor again and again uses up all 378 coconuts: three blocks of 20 groups and one of 3 groups.
images.description: A bar of 378 coconuts shown as three blocks of 120 (20 groups of 6) and one block of 18 (3 groups of 6).
images.context: Concept image for Take Away Groups of the Divisor. The numbers are the plan's own worked example, not a number of any book question; the bar is not drawn to scale.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student how many groups were taken away in all. The slip to watch: thinking each block is one group instead of 20 groups.

image_decisions.why: The bar of blocks is the mathematics of taking away groups of the divisor again and again.
